tag: Sprint 14 Task E, F117 (F114 cloud read)

solver-selection-cvqls: Section II-D, p.3: the authors state their own choice of CVQLS, after Table I and the note that later sections compare VQLS and CVQLS
opf-formulation-setup: Section III-A, p.3: states the ACOPF and DCOPF formulations used, as in MATPOWER [26]
qipm-structure-setup: Section III, p.3 and p.5-6: states how CVQLS is integrated in IPM and the hybrid split; the Fig. 1 text says each IPM iteration needs CVQLS iterations
pauli-decomposition-encoding: Section III-C, p.4: states the choice of Pauli decomposition and why; Section V-C, p.9 mentions padding to make the matrix Hermitian
ansatz-selection-procedure: Section IV-B, p.7: states its own empirical selection procedure and that two ansatzes are in Fig. 3
realhw-2bus-setup: Section V-D, p.10: states the 2-bus system, 100 MW load, 7x7 padded to 8x8 and the four-qubit circuit (3 solution qubits plus flag)
realhw-only-2bus: Section V-D, p.10: states real hardware was used only for the 2-bus case and simulators for the rest, because of noise and time
simulator-capacity-limit: Section V-A, p.9 and V-E, p.11: states the simulator capacity limit, out-of-memory on 118- and 300-bus with 16 GB RAM, and that more simulation is needed
mu-correction-method: Section IV-E, p.8, Algorithm II, Fig. 4: defines its own barrier-parameter fixing rule (relDif threshold or +/-20% deviation over the last few iterations, otherwise classical update). Eqs. (19)-(20) are lost in the text layer, but the rule is stated in words
complexity-assumes-fault-tolerance: Section IV-F, p.8: the authors state the complexity estimate assumes fault-tolerant hardware and a suitable KKT matrix, and call the outcomes theoretical upper-bound demonstrations
review-vqa-definition: Section 1, p.4: the review states what a VQA is (parameterized circuit prepares a state, cost from measurement, classical optimizer). An introductory definition with citation [25], accepted as the paper's definition of the term
review-fig6-burgers-setup: Section 3.2.4, p.22-23 and Fig. 6 caption, p.24: states the Burgers setup with Dirichlet conditions, sin initial condition, 20-neuron layers, five-qubit angle-cascading circuit, classical five-layer PINN and FDM comparison
review-scope-qubit-based: Section 3.2.2, p.19 states the review focuses on qubit-based computing (CV noted as alternative); Section 1, p.5 states Burgers illustrations and code are on GitHub
qpatch-baselines-definition: Section III-G, p.5: RBF-SVM on the same 8-dim input, Tiny CNN with at most 100k parameters on spectrograms
qpatch-patch-summary-definition: Section III-D, Eqs. (5)-(11), p.3: defines the four summary features of each 4x4 patch
qpatch-front-end-setup: Section III-C, Eqs. (1)-(4), p.2: 16 kHz, 64 mel bins, 25 ms Hann, 10 ms hop, 1024-point FFT, per-utterance standardization
qpatch-top-k-selection: Section III-D, Eqs. (12)-(13), p.4: ranks by s1 and keeps the top two, concatenated to x in R8
qpatch-top-k-limitation: Section III-D, p.4: the authors say they do not claim mean activation is optimal and leave sensitivity to future work
qpatch-feature-map-definition: Section III-E, Eqs. (14)-(18), p.4: RX, RY, RZ, RY rotations, CZ chain, and a CZ(q3,q4) between the two blocks
qpatch-feature-map-no-trainable-paramete: Section III-E p.4 and III-F p.5: summaries used directly as angles, no variational parameters, no iterative circuit optimization
qpatch-fidelity-kernel-definition: Section III-E Eq. (19), III-F Eqs. (20)-(21), p.4-5: defines the fidelity kernel, the Gram matrix and the precomputed-kernel SVM
qpatch-circuit-depth-bound: Section III-E, p.4: depth limited to d<=3, parallel rotations, local CZ chains
qpatch-metric-definition: Section III-G(c), Eq. (22), p.5: defines AUROC and EER; Section IV-A reports them on the 20-sample dev split
qpatch-preliminary-evidence-no-uncertain: Section IV-A, p.6: gains are called preliminary; repeated splits and confidence intervals are left to future work
qpatch-spoof-generation-limit: Section IV-F(a), p.7: noise and spectral distortion do not cover replay, neural TTS or voice conversion
qpatch-hardware-gap-limit: Section IV-F(c), p.7: only ideal simulation; noise and finite shots not studied
qpatch-no-ablation-limit: Section IV-F(d), p.7: a broader ablation was not feasible within compute and page budget
qpatch-simulation-environment: Section III-H, p.5: CPU-only simulation, Python, scikit-learn, an unnamed quantum simulation framework
qpatch-no-emissions-estimate: Section IV-G, p.8: no direct emissions estimate was made
qpatch-dataset-setup: Section III-B, p.2: 100 balanced LJ Speech samples (50/50), noise and spectral-distortion spoofs, 80/20 split; the stored value matches
qpatch-limits: Section IV-A p.6 (20-sample dev split, point estimates) and Section III-H p.5 (no hardware runs, ideal simulation): the authors' own statements; the stored value matches
fraudtransformer-model-configuration: Section 6 and Table 2, p.4: GPT-style, 6 blocks, 8 heads, context 1024, embedding 512, about 20M parameters, vocabulary about 4000
fraudtransformer-training-objective: Section 6, p.4: binary cross entropy, absolute and relative timestamps, attention unchanged
fraudtransformer-dataset-description: Section 4, p.3: states the dataset content, more than 10 numerical and more than 10 categorical features, features withheld, last 500 events
fraudtransformer-data-splits: Section 4, p.3: temporal test split, validation sampled from training, 332,000 samples, about 60/30/10
fraudtransformer-encoding-process: Section 5, p.3: grouping, binning, vocabulary about 4000, no sub-word tokens, per-column tokens plus column embedding
fraudtransformer-time-id-definitions: Section 3 p.3 and Section 6 p.4: defines the absolute and relative time-ids and the token-level and event-level schemes
fraudtransformer-time-encoder-design: Section 3 p.2 and Section 6 p.4-5: time encoders reuse sinusoidal and rotary encoders with time-ids; LayerNorm only on the time embedding; GPT-2-style learned positions without LayerNorm; all added to the residual stream
fraudtransformer-hyperparameter-protocol: Section 7.3, p.5: time gain and base frequency tuned; one epoch per pair, validated at end of epoch one
fraudtransformer-baselines-description: Section 7.2, p.5 and footnote 1, p.6: baseline descriptions, same features, L2 logistic regression with grid search, no subsampling for the trees
fraudtransformer-baseline-features-snaps: Section 7.6, p.6: states the baseline features come from a single time snapshot for these comparisons
fraudtransformer-ablation-design: Section 7.5, p.5 and Table 1: architecture, optimization, splits and preprocessing fixed; time encoder, scheme, positional encoder and LayerNorm varied
fraudtransformer-prauc-baseline: Section 7.7, p.6: the authors state the PRAUC chance level equals the positive rate (0.43 here) and that they report relative differences; this is their reporting protocol, not a result
fraudtransformer-fraud-subtype-setup: Section 7.4, p.5: subtype-specific test sets with non-fraud plus one subtype; the best model is evaluated; AUROC and PR-AUC reported
fraudtransformer-future-work: Section 8, p.7: the authors state the work uses BCE only and name pre-training, multi-class and larger context as future work
fraudtransformer-disclaimer: Disclaimer, p.7: states the paper is not an HSBC product and was reviewed by HSBC's publication clearance team
fraudtransformer-evaluation-set-undersam: Section 4, p.3 and Section 7.7, p.6: the evaluation set was sampled to conceal the fraud rate, about 43% fraud by undersampling, results may differ at other rates; the stored value matches
study-configuration-52-cases: Introduction, p.3: states the results cover 52 configurations (1-, 2-, 2-entangled qubit; four optimizers; two costs; two patterns; fixed and random data)
data-generation-circle-balanced: Results, p.3: circle task with radius giving equal areas, 50% chance accuracy, fixed seed for fixed data, new random data for each of 20 iterations, averaged
training-test-sizes-and-overfit-filter: Results, p.3-4: training sizes up to 250, overfitting results removed so 50 to 250 shown, 4000-point test set in the single-qubit section
five-layer-choice-and-desktop-simulation: Results, p.3-4: 5 layers chosen from runs with 1 to 5 layers aiming at about 90% test accuracy, desktop feasibility, used for all cases (Supp. Figs S1.1, S1.2)
trace-distance-only-one-qubit-fidelity-o: Results, p.5-6: two-qubit and entangled studies focus on fidelity with Nelder-Mead after Figure 4, and the random-data study also uses fidelity
entangled-classifier-cz-after-each-layer: Method, p.12, Fig. 14(e): the entangled classifier is the two-qubit classifier with a CZ after each layer
limit-synthetic-data-and-planned-compari: Introduction, p.2: the authors state that real-data-like random sets, fixed-versus-random comparisons and comparison with other QML are still to do
future-work-complex-systems: Discussion, p.11: the authors state extension to more complex systems and broader tasks as future work
code-trace-cost-maximises-distance-to-la: Supplementary Note 8 (trace_minimization.py, p.35-39): Av_Tr is the mean of trace_dis (half the norm of the Bloch difference) and the scipy cost returns -Av_Tr; the classifier returns np.argmax of the distances; two-class label states are opposite Bloch vectors. A literal reading of the listing; it does not show the results used this code. The sign convention is notable (minimising maximises distance)
reupload-future-work-real-data: Discussion, p.11: the garbled sentence says real-world data sets will be considered in their next research work, so they are not covered here

theory_low.review-parameter-shift-cost: Section 2.1, p.8: O(2mS) is stated in a sentence with no derivation; the counting is not proved here
theory_low.review-mpo-bond-dimension-three: Section 4, Step 2, p.32: bond dimension 3 is stated and the MPO tensors are listed (eqs. 64-70), but there is no proof or check that they reproduce D(1) and D(2); a construction asserted, not a proved result
theory_low.review-mps-hadamard-bond-growth: Section 4, Step 2, p.33: eqs. (72)-(73) show the construction, but the bond-dimension growth is a standard fact stated in prose, not a theorem with a proof
